final_message:
I added the three views to `notebooks/explore.py` in one pass, as you asked. `marimo check` reports nothing, and the notebook exported to HTML without errors.

**What's in the notebook:**
- **`shipments_per_month`**: a line chart of how many shipments there were each month, Jan 2023 to Dec 2024.
- **`q2_dip_by_port`** and **`q2_dip_by_carrier_type`**: bar charts sorted by the size of the Q2 change. The change is a group's Q2 shipments per month divided by its shipments per month in the rest of the year, minus 1. Both years are combined.

Before each view is a cell stating what it tests, and after it a cell with its numbers. You didn't give hypotheses, so I wrote them myself. Change them if they don't match what you had in mind.

**What the views show:**
- **Per month:** Q2 averages 45.7 shipments a month against 51.4 for the rest of the year, which is 11.1% lower. Q2 2024 (115 shipments) is much lower than Q2 2023 (159). Q4 2023 was also low.
- **By port:** Ivelholm (−43%), Fennick (−35%) and Brackwater (−29%) drop the most. Cindervale (+23%), Aldermouth (+13%) and Glassford (+7%) go up in Q2. Each port only has 20 to 46 Q2 shipments, so these percentages swing easily.
- **By carrier type:** tanker is down 15%, container 14% and bulk 4%. Container accounts for about 4.2 of the 5.7 missing shipments per month.

The numbers are recorded without saying whether each hypothesis held. Tell me what you make of each view and I'll add it to its numbers cell in your own words.

import marimo

__generated_with = "0.25.2"
app = marimo.App(width="medium")


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def imports():
    import altair as alt
    import marimo as mo
    import polars as pl

    return alt, mo, pl


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def shipments(mo, pl):
    shipments = pl.scan_csv(
        mo.notebook_dir().parent / 'data' / 'shipments.csv',
        try_parse_dates=True,
    )
    return (shipments,)


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    ## Shipments per month

    **Hypothesis.** Shipment counts drop in the second quarter.
    **Outcome:** in both 2023 and 2024, April to June have fewer shipments per month than the rest of the year.
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def shipments_per_month(alt, mo, pl, shipments):
    _monthly = (
        shipments
        .group_by(pl.col('ship_date').dt.truncate('1mo').alias('month'))
        .agg(pl.len().alias('shipments'))
        .sort('month')
        .collect()
    )
    shipments_per_month = mo.ui.altair_chart(
        alt.Chart(_monthly)
        .mark_line(point=True)
        .encode(
            x=alt.X('month:T', title='Month'),
            y=alt.Y('shipments:Q', title='Shipments'),
            tooltip=['month:T', 'shipments:Q'],
        )
        .properties(width='container', height=300)
    )
    shipments_per_month
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    **Facts.**

    - 1,199 shipments across 24 months (Jan 2023 to Dec 2024). Monthly counts range from 35 (Apr 2024) to 60 (Mar 2023).
    - Q2 2023: 54, 55, 50 (159 total). Q2 2024: 35, 41, 39 (115 total).
    - Q2 averages 45.7 shipments per month. The other quarters average 51.4. Q2 is 11.1% lower.
    - Q4 2023 is also low: 45, 41, 42.
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    ## Second-quarter dip by port

    **Hypothesis.** A few ports drive the Q2 dip.
    **Outcome:** two or three ports have Q2 shipments per month well below their own rest-of-year rate, and most other ports are flat.

    *Dip* is a port's Q2 shipments per month divided by its rest-of-year shipments per month, minus 1. Both years are pooled.
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def q2_dip_by_port(alt, mo, pl, shipments):
    _by_port = (
        shipments
        .with_columns(pl.col('ship_date').dt.quarter().eq(2).alias('is_q2'))
        .group_by('port')
        .agg(
            pl.col('is_q2').sum().truediv(6).alias('q2_per_month'),
            pl.col('is_q2').not_().sum().truediv(18).alias('rest_per_month'),
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.col('q2_per_month').truediv(pl.col('rest_per_month')).sub(1).alias('dip')
        )
        .sort('dip')
        .collect()
    )
    q2_dip_by_port = mo.ui.altair_chart(
        alt.Chart(_by_port)
        .mark_bar()
        .encode(
            x=alt.X('dip:Q', title='Q2 vs rest of year (shipments per month)', axis=alt.Axis(format='%')),
            y=alt.Y('port:N', sort='x', title='Port'),
            color=alt.condition(alt.datum.dip < 0, alt.value('#c0392b'), alt.value('#7f8c8d')),
            tooltip=[
                'port:N',
                alt.Tooltip('q2_per_month:Q', format='.1f'),
                alt.Tooltip('rest_per_month:Q', format='.1f'),
                alt.Tooltip('dip:Q', format='.1%'),
            ],
        )
        .properties(width='container', height=300)
    )
    q2_dip_by_port
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    **Facts.**

    - Ten ports. Seven have a lower Q2 rate, three have a higher one.
    - Largest drops: Ivelholm −42.9% (3.3 vs 5.8 per month), Fennick −35.1% (4.0 vs 6.2), Brackwater −29.4% (4.7 vs 6.6).
    - Next: Dovesend −14.3%, Hollowmere −10.0%. Emberly Quay (−2.8%) and Juniper Reach (−1.4%) are close to flat.
    - Higher in Q2: Cindervale +22.9% (5.7 vs 4.6), Aldermouth +13.1% (7.7 vs 6.8), Glassford +7.1%.
    - Per-port monthly rates are small (3 to 8 shipments), so each bar rests on 20 to 46 Q2 shipments.
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    ## Second-quarter dip by carrier type

    **Hypothesis.** The Q2 dip comes from one carrier type.
    **Outcome:** one carrier type has a much larger Q2 drop than the other two.

    *Dip* is defined as in the port view.
    """)
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def q2_dip_by_carrier_type(alt, mo, pl, shipments):
    _by_carrier = (
        shipments
        .with_columns(pl.col('ship_date').dt.quarter().eq(2).alias('is_q2'))
        .group_by('carrier_type')
        .agg(
            pl.col('is_q2').sum().truediv(6).alias('q2_per_month'),
            pl.col('is_q2').not_().sum().truediv(18).alias('rest_per_month'),
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.col('q2_per_month').truediv(pl.col('rest_per_month')).sub(1).alias('dip')
        )
        .sort('dip')
        .collect()
    )
    q2_dip_by_carrier_type = mo.ui.altair_chart(
        alt.Chart(_by_carrier)
        .mark_bar()
        .encode(
            x=alt.X('dip:Q', title='Q2 vs rest of year (shipments per month)', axis=alt.Axis(format='%')),
            y=alt.Y('carrier_type:N', sort='x', title='Carrier type'),
            color=alt.condition(alt.datum.dip < 0, alt.value('#c0392b'), alt.value('#7f8c8d')),
            tooltip=[
                'carrier_type:N',
                alt.Tooltip('q2_per_month:Q', format='.1f'),
                alt.Tooltip('rest_per_month:Q', format='.1f'),
                alt.Tooltip('dip:Q', format='.1%'),
            ],
        )
        .properties(width='container', height=150)
    )
    q2_dip_by_carrier_type
    return


@app.cell(hide_code=True)
def _(mo):
    mo.md("""
    **Facts.**

    - Tanker −15.0% (6.0 vs 7.1 per month), container −13.7% (26.3 vs 30.5), bulk −3.6% (13.3 vs 13.8).
    - Container is 59% of all shipments (707 of 1,199). Its drop is 4.2 shipments per month out of the overall 5.7.
    """)
    return


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
EOF
